page.layout: Two engraved medallions side by side at the top, each with a portrait and a legend; below them one column of running text; no margin notes; signature at the foot right; running head and page number at the top.

main_text.l: ORESTES occiso Ægistho imperat Mycoenis, quæ urbs
est in Peloponneso, anno mundi 2789. ante Christum natum
1173. Fuit hic Agamemnonis & Clytemnestræ filius: matrem
adulteram cum adultero suo Ægistho interemit, quòd patrem
suum etiam interemerat. Deinde Pyrrhum quoque interfecit,
quòd Hermionem sibi prius desponsatam, quæ & Pyrrhum
oderat, rapuisset, víque eam in uxorem sibi retinuisset. Ob hæc
scelera furiis agitatus vagabatur: habuit interim Pyladem fi-
dum itineris comitem ac periculorum socium. Pervenit itaque
Orestes in regionem Tauricam, ubi inventa sorore Electra,
cum ea, jam furore purgatus, migravit in Italiam. Orestes pro
Pylade, Pylades pro Oreste, uterque pro altero mori minimè
recusavit: sicut nec Nysus pro Eurialo, nec Eurialus pro Nyso,
uti est apud Verg. quare numeratur inter insigniora amicorum
paria. Vide Sophocl. in Electra, Euripid. in Oreste, Cicer. de ami-
citia, & lib. 2. de finib. Ovid. Epist. 8. Heroidum.
HERMIONE Menelaï & Helenæ filia fuit. Hæc à Tyn-
daro avo materno primùm pacta est in uxorem Oresti, interea
dum pater in bello Troiano militaret: qui etiam eandem Pyr-
rho, mortuo patre Achille, promittit. Pyrrhus reversus eam
rapit, ac retinet invitam: quamobrem indignatus Orestes Pyr-
rhum in templo Apollinis, ope Macarei sacerdotis interficit,
uxorémque suam Hermionem recipit. Videto Vergil. libr. 3.
Aeneid. Ovid. epist. 8. supradicta, quæ inscribitur, Hermione
Oresti.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions (roundels) at the top of the page, not text. Left: a helmeted profile portrait labelled with a legend reading roughly "ORESTES AGA·MEMNONIS" (partly [?]). Right: a female profile portrait with a legend reading roughly "HERMIONE" and "MENELAI" (partly [?]). The legends are part of the engraving and are not transcribed as text. Line-end break "ami/citia" in "amicitia": no printed hyphen, so written whole. Numbers "2 7 8 9" and "1 1 7 3" are printed with wide letter spacing; copied as 2789 and 1173. Spelling u/v and i/j normalised as instructed (e.g. vxorem to uxorem, inuenta to inventa, Ouid. to Ovid.).
